title: The Vale Investigation · Lilacs and the Living Barrier
dek: Mara Vale asks adventurers to learn where her husband goes. Flowers and an obsession lead the company beyond Pristinia, where a memorial and a living obstruction leave the answer out of reach.

facts.Setting: Pristinia; market shops; unnamed woods beyond the town
facts.People: Clive L. Dragoon; Di’trillio; Saoirse; Vylaris Monry; Felicity; Mara and Elias Vale
facts.Outcome: Investigation ongoing at a living barrier; three blue lights approach

body:
The request sounds small beside a war. A wife believes her husband has fallen in love with someone else, and several adventurers wonder why she needs a whole company to investigate it. Yet Mara Vale has kept a place for Elias at their table while his absences have lengthened. Nobody else will take her concern seriously. Clive, Di’trillio, Saoirse, Vylaris and Felicity answer.

The place she keeps for him

Mara welcomes them into a modest, carefully tended house within Pristinia’s walls. Flowers stand by the window. The unused place at the table has gathered dust. She says Elias, a day laborer, has stopped coming home for meals and no longer spends his leisure time with the friends she knows. Whatever happiness he finds elsewhere has not been shared with her.

The company questions her gently and less gently. Saoirse offers ordinary explanations: friends, cards, shopping. Clive asks whether she has spoken to Elias. Di’trillio wonders why she has turned to volatile adventurers rather than an investigator. Mara’s answer is that she had no one else. The narrator confirms that her fear and concern are sincere.

Felicity asks permission to examine the vanity and his clothes, hoping to find a trace of another visitor. Vylaris searches for magic. Neither investigation supplies the explanation they want. There is no detected magic in the house; the vanity holds simple grooming things rather than expensive perfume. What the rooms show most clearly is Mara’s continuing effort to keep a home ready for someone who seldom returns.

Pressed about his routine, she admits that Elias has not been working. He has been buying gifts in the market, and those gifts do not come home to her. The company decides to follow him there.

Lilacs instead of lilies

The market is crowded enough for the adventurers to follow without immediately exposing themselves. Felicity and Di’trillio help find the hurried man. Saoirse listens to his thoughts and shares the urgency she hears: someone is waiting, and he believes he is late.

He enters a florist’s shop. Felicity follows in the familiar guise of a maid shopping for her employer, asking about romantic flowers while trying to encourage revealing conversation. Di’trillio slips into another row, briefly looking for hydrangeas for Vessalia. Even while investigating another couple’s trouble, he is thinking about the person he loves.

Elias wants his usual bouquet. Saoirse’s glimpses of his thoughts settle on lilacs, chosen for someone other than Mara, who likes lilies. The woman in those thoughts is indistinct. Saoirse suspects concealment, but the blurred image does not establish a particular spell or identity. Vylaris finds no enchantment on Elias and no useful magic in the shop.

The florist is initially unwilling to gossip. After Elias leaves and returns for his forgotten money, Felicity gets a little more: the man has known the Vales since their wedding and cannot reconcile this behavior with the husband he remembers. He suspects enchantment. That is his explanation, offered by someone fond of Mara; the company’s magical search has not confirmed it. Elias leaves with the flowers and hurries onward.

Following him does not settle the argument

Elias buys honey cakes and makes another stop before setting out for the woods. His impatience unsettles the shopkeepers as much as the people following him. Clive’s anger grows: he wants to confront the man, and considers bringing him straight back to his wife. Saoirse argues for discovering who waits for him first.

Vylaris finds the whole situation uncomfortable. Love seems to him an uncontrolled variable, capable of making someone as miserable as Mara. Di’trillio pushes back. He once believed he should live only as a weapon, he says, until Vessalia showed him another possibility. The risk of being hurt does not make every loving relationship worthless. Their discussion continues while the investigation is supposed to remain discreet.

In the woods, Elias hears them. Felicia appears like a forest phantom, attempting to preserve the others’ concealment, but Di’trillio steps out and demands an answer. Elias first cowers, then admits his consuming desire for Nhalis. He insists she needs him and that he cannot help his feelings.

Di’trillio does not accept that as an excuse for abandoning Mara without an explanation. He knows what it means to need someone, he says, and still asks what Elias owes his wife. The company follows him farther, without deciding that sincere desire proves either harmless love or supernatural compulsion.

Three lights beyond the questions

The forest grows quiet. A weathered carving shows three figures holding small flames, and a warning asks that the dead be given peace. Farther on, another memorial asks travelers to speak forgotten names and pray where bodies rest. Elias reads Claire, Ethan and Emily from the stone. He says it predates his meetings with Nhalis.

Ahead, roots, moss and decaying growth have swallowed the path. Running water can be heard beyond it. Elias says the obstruction was not there before. Felicity asks whether Nhalis is dead; he denies it. Vylaris wonders about possession. Those questions remain questions.

Felicity cleans the neglected stones. Saoirse prays for the named dead. The company learns that the growth behaves like a living organism rather than ordinary roots. Di’trillio sheathes his blades instead of immediately cutting into it. Saoirse addresses it and asks for passage.

It does not move. Three blue orbs appear and approach the company. Saoirse wonders whether they are souls; Clive calls them wisps, but the account stops as further knowledge is being sought. The travelers have found more than an ordinary shopping trip, yet they have not met Nhalis or resolved Mara’s marriage. The barrier and the approaching lights are where this part of the investigation ends.
